name: City Council Meeting - Jan 23, 2024
agenda_text:
TORRANCE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  JANUARY 23, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING
  5:00 P.M. - CLOSED SESSION
  6:30 P.M. - REGULAR BUSINESS BEGINS
  IN COUNCIL CHAMBER AT 3031 TORRANCE BL.

  CITY COUNCIL MAY TAKE ACTION ON ANY ITEM LISTED ON THE AGENDA

City Council Agenda 01-23-24

OPENING CEREMONIES

OPENING CEREMONIES

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  14A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION (California
  Government Code §54956.9(d)(1)):
  1)  City of Whittier, et al. v. Superior Court of the State of California, County of Los
  Angeles, et al. LASC Case No. 23STCP03579
  2)  Sling Flying Club, LLC, DBA Sling Pilot Academy v. City of Torrance, et al.  LASC
  Case No. 23STCP04538
  3)  Sling Flying Club, LLC d/b/a Sling Pilot Academy v. City of Torrance, California  FAA
  Docket No. 16-23-20
  14A - STAFF REPORT

  14B. REAL PROPERTY – CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR
  (California Government Code §54956.8):
  1)  Property: 3481 Airport Drive, #200, Torrance, CA 90505 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Torrance Flite Park, LLC Under
  Negotiation: Terms and conditions of lease
  2)  Property: 1345 Post Avenue, Torrance, CA 90501 Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan
  Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Torrance Historical Society Under Negotiation:
  Terms and conditions of lease
  3)  Property: 4111 Pacific Coast Highway, Torrance, CA 90505 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Vivo Investments Under
  Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease
  4)  Property: 2300 Carson Street, Torrance, CA 90501 Agency Negotiator: Aram
  Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and Los Angeles County Under
  Negotiation: Price and terms and conditions of lease

  14C. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (California Government Code
  §54957.6): Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Employee
  Organization/Association:
  1. Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees
  2. Certain Part-Time Hourly Employees
  3. Crossing Guards
  4. Elected Officials
  5. Engineers and Torrance Fiscal Employees Association

  7. Police & Fire Trainees

  10. Fire Safety Management
   11. Torrance Fire Fighters Association
  12. Torrance Library Employees Association
  13. Torrance Municipal Employees/AFSCME Local 1117 AFL-CIO
  14. Torrance Police Commanders Association (TPCA)
  15. Torrance Police Officers Association
  16. Torrance Professional Parks & Recreation Employees Organization
  17. Torrance Professional & Supervisory Association
  18. Torrance Recurrent Recreational Employees Organization
  19. City Treasurer
  20. City Clerk
  21. City Attorney
  22. City Manager

RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION - Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9 (d)(1)

RECONVENED IN PUBLIC SESSION

2.  FLAG SALUTE: Councilmember Mattucci

NON SECTARIAN INVOCATION: Councilmember Sheikh

3.  REPORT OF THE CITY CLERK ON THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA The agenda was
  posted on the Public Notice Board at 3031 Torrance Bl. and on the City’s Website on
  Wednesday, January 17, 2024 /s/ Rebecca Poirier

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READING OF RESOLUTIONS AND ORDINANCES AFTER
NUMBER & TITLE – See Council Rules of Order Section 2.11 (Resolution 2006-65)

4.  ANNOUNCEMENT OF WITHDRAWN, DEFERRED, AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL ITEMS

5.  COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

6.  COMMUNITY MATTERS

  6A. PROCLAMATION honoring Torrance Centenarian Catherine Uchenwa Ogbuka.
  6A - STAFF REPORT

  6B. City Clerk – Appoint Member to Fill Unscheduled Planning Commission Vacancy.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council review applications and appoint
  member to fill an unscheduled vacancy on the Planning Commission from a list of qualified
  applicants. The City Clerk will administer the Oath of Office to the newly appointed
  commissioner if present.
  6B - STAFF REPORT

7.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #1 (Limited up to a 15 minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comment on items under the Consent Calendar or items that
  are not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council cannot act on
  items raised during public comment, but may respond briefly to statements made or
  questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item to staff. Speakers under Orals
  are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral Communications #2 and no
  longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you step up to the microphone.
  Speakers please turn off or leave your cellular phone when you come to the
  microphone to speak. If presenting handout material to Council, please provide 11
  copies to the City Clerk before speaking.
  PUBLIC COMMENT
  PUBLIC COMMENT RECEIVED AFTER 5:30 P.M. ON 01/22/24 AND BEFORE 1:56 A.M.
  ON 01/24/24

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..
   8A. City Clerk – Approve City Council Minutes. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Clerk that City Council approve the City Council minutes of
  December 12, 2023, December 18, 2023, December 19, 2023 and January 9, 2024.

  8B. Public Works and General Services – Appropriate Funds and Authorize Change
  Order #1 to Purchase Order #2023-00000388 for Nine (9) 2024 Ford F-150 Trucks.
  Expenditure: $56,620.77 (Non-General Funds).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director and General Services Director that City
  Council:
  1) Appropriate $1,827.52 from the Sewer Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fund balance to the
  Sewer Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fiscal year 2023-24 operating budget; and
  2) Appropriate $43,828.11 from the Sanitation Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fund balance
  to the Sanitation Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fiscal year 2023-24 operating budget;
  and
  3) Appropriate $3,655.04 from the Water Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fund balance to the
  Water Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fiscal year 2023-24 operating budget; and
  4) Appropriate $7,310.10 from the Fleet Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fund balance to the
  Fleet Vehicle Replacement Fund’s fiscal year 2023-24 operating budget; and
  5) Authorize change order #1 with National Auto Fleet Group of Watsonville, CA
  (PO#2023-00000388) in the amount of $56,620.77, including sales tax, for a new not-
  to-exceed amount of $378,005.31, for the purchase of nine (9) 2024 Ford F-150 trucks.
  8B - STAFF REPORT

  8C. Human Resources – Approve Changes to Employee Referral Program.
  Expenditure: Approximately $66,400 (General Fund and Non-General Funds).
  Recommendation of the Human Resources Director that City Council approve the changes
  to the Employee Referral Program in the amount of approximately $66,400 through January
  31, 2025.
  8C - STAFF REPORT

9.  ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS

  9A. City Manager – Review Findings of Land Use Study for 13 City-Owned Properties
  and Provide Direction on Potential Property Disposition Opportunities.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Review Findings of Land Use Study for 13 City-Owned Properties; and
  2) Provide Direction on Potential Property Disposition Opportunities.
  9A - STAFF REPORT
  9A - STAFF PRESENTATION
  9A - SUPPLEMENTAL

  9B. City Manager – Discuss and Provide Direction on Potential Land Use Study for
  Torrance Municipal Airport – Zamperini Field. Expenditure: None. In response to
  an oral request by Councilmember Jon Kaji with City Council concurrence, it is
  the recommendation of the City Manager that City Council discuss and provide
  direction on options for a potential Land Use Study for the Torrance Municipal
  Airport – Zamperini Field.
  9B - STAFF REPORT
  9B - SUPPLEMENTAL
  PUBLIC COMMENT RECEIVED AFTER 5:30 P.M. ON 01/22/24 AND BEFORE 1:56
  A.M. ON 01/24/24

  9C. Public Works – Adopt RESOLUTION Approving and Authorizing the Public Works
  Director to Execute Cooperative Implementation Agreement and Accept and
  Appropriate $2,000,000 Settlement Contribution for Torrance Airport Storm Water
  Basin Project, I-174. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council:
  1) Adopt a RESOLUTION approving and authorizing the Public Works Director to execute
  cooperative implementation agreement #D43CIATOA0001 with the California
  Department of Transportation for the Torrance Airport Storm Water Basin Project, I-174;
  and
   2)  Upon execution of cooperative implementation agreement #D43CIATOA0001, accept
  and appropriate a settlement contribution in the amount of $2,000,000 to the Torrance
  Airport Storm Water Basin Project, I-174.
  9C - STAFF REPORT

9D. Public Works – Approve First Amendment to Consulting Services Agreement for
  Torrance Airport Storm Water Basin Project, I-174. Expenditure: $46,430 (Non-
  General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council approve a first amendment
  to the consulting services agreement with Tetra Tech, Inc. of Irvine, CA (C2022-009) in the
  amount of $46,430, for a new not-to-exceed amount of $832,352, to provide preliminary and
  final design services for the Torrance Airport Stormwater Basin Project, I-174 and to extend
  the term for an additional two-year period beginning January 25, 2024 and ending January
  24, 2026.
  9D - STAFF REPORT

9E.  Public Works – Approve Specifications, Appropriate Funds, Award Public Works
  Agreement, and Adopt Categorical Exemption Under California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) Section 15301(c) – Existing Facilities (Class 1) for Sidewalk
  Repair for Disabled Accessibility, I-135. Expenditure: $1,171,792.50 (Non-General
  Funds).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council:
  1) Approve the specifications for the Sidewalk Repair for Disabled Accessibility, I-135
  (B2023-36); and
  2) Appropriate $106,598 of Transportation Development Act (TDA) Article 3 funds to the
  Sidewalk Repair for Disabled Accessibility, I-135, and authorize any future interest
  earned on these funds to also be appropriated to the project; and
  3) Award a public works agreement to Kalban, Inc. of Santa Clarita, CA (B2023-36) in the
  amount of $1,018,950 and authorize a 15% contingency in the amount of $152,842.50
  for construction of the Sidewalk Repair for Disabled Accessibility, I-135 for a two-year
  period beginning January 23, 2024, and ending January 22, 2026; and
  4) Adopt a finding that the project is categorically exempt under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section
  15301(c) – Existing Facilities (Class 1) and that there are no features that distinguish
  this project from others in exempt class, and therefore, there are no unusual
  circumstances.
  9E - STAFF REPORT

9F.  City Manager and Community Services – Approve Grant Agreement, Accept and
  Appropriate $5,000,000 Grant Award, and Appoint Members to Advisory
  Committee for World War II Camp Wall Monument Project at Columbia Park.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager and Community Services Director that City Council:
  1) Approve grant agreement #GF2126-0 with the California Natural Resources Agency for
  the World War II Camp Wall Monument project at Columbia Park; and
  2) Upon execution of grant agreement #GF2126-0, accept and appropriate a grant
  program award in the amount of $5,000,000; and
  3) Appoint three (3) members to fill the five-member advisory committee to provide
  consultation for the project.
  9F - STAFF REPORT

9G. Finance and Governmental Operations Committee – Approve Committee’s
  Recommendations Regarding Various Revenue Enhancement Opportunities and
  Creation of Community Facilities District. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Finance and Governmental Operations Committee that City
  Council:
  1) Approve the Committee’s recommendation regarding various revenue enhancement
  opportunities; and
  2) Approve the Committee’s recommendation regarding the creation of a community
  facilities district.
  9G - STAFF REPORT
  9G - STAFF PRESENTATION
  9G - SUPPLEMENTAL
   9H. Community Development – Discuss and Consider Adopting ORDINANCE
  Amending Torrance Municipal Code Regulating Touch (and Stop) and Go, Full
  Stop-Taxi Back and Low Approaches at Torrance Municipal Airport and Adopt
  California Environmental Quality Act Exemption. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council:
  1) Discuss and consider amending the Torrance Municipal Airport (Airport) Ordinance to
  regulate touch (and stop) and go, full stop-taxi back, and low approaches at the Airport;
  and
  2) Adopt an ORDINANCE amending Torrance Municipal Code (TMC) Article 5 “Touch
  (and Stop) and Go, Full Stop-Taxi Back and Low Approaches” of Chapter 1, Division 5;
  and
  3) Adopt a California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) exemption per guidelines §15378
  and 15061(b)(3); and
  4) Approve an Ordinance Summary for publication.
  9H - STAFF REPORT
  9H - SUPPLEMENTAL
  PUBLIC COMMENT RECEIVED AFTER 5:30 P.M. ON 01/22/24 AND BEFORE 1:56
  A.M. ON 01/24/24

  9I.  City Manager – Appoint Chair and Members to City Council Ad Hoc Facility
  Naming Committee. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that the Mayor appoints Chair and Members to City
  Council Ad Hoc Facility Naming Committee.
  9I - STAFF REPORT

  9J.  City Manager – Receive Update on Public Health Department Research.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council receive a Public Health Department
  Research update.
  9J - STAFF REPORT
  9J - STAFF PRESENTATION
  9J - MATERIALS AVAILABLE

10.  HEARINGS – None Scheduled.

11.  AGENCY AGENDAS – None Scheduled.

12.  2ND READING ORDINANCES – None Scheduled.

RECESS

RECONVENE

13.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #2 (Limited up to a 15 minute period) Council Order –
  Sheikh, Griffiths, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Mayor Chen This portion of the meeting
  is reserved for comment on items not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act,
  City Council cannot act on items raised during public comment, but may respond
  briefly to statements made or questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item
  to staff. Speakers under Orals are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral
  Communications #2 and no longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you
  step up to the microphone. Speakers please turn off or leave your cellular phone
  when you come to the microphone to speak. If presenting handout material to
  Council, please provide 11 copies to the City Clerk before speaking.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  RECONVENE

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  15A. Adjournment of City Council meeting to Tuesday, February 6, 2024, at 5:00 p.m.
  for closed session, with regular business commencing at 6:30 p.m. in the
  Council Chamber. Tuesday, January 30, 2024, is a Council Dark Night.
 15 - STAFF REPORT
